LJ2K: pad lossy chunks so that wavelet folds stay on low-pass positions (#2633)

* LJ2K: pad lossy chunks so that wavelet folds stay on low-pass positions

Every LJ2K chunk (or tile) is coded as an independent HTJ2K codestream
with image origin (0, 0).  With the whole-sample symmetric extension of
JPEG 2000, a chunk dimension that is even at any decomposition level
places the fold of the extension on a high-pass position; the
quantization error of the resulting coefficient shows up as a visible
step on the last row (or last column) of the chunk.  On a smooth
gradient the last row of a 256-row chunk is about 10-15 dB below the
interior rows; the same happens on the last column of an even-width
image and on every tile boundary of tiled files.

The fold lands on a low-pass position at all L levels if and only if
the coded length is congruent to 1 modulo 2^L.  For lossy coding the
encoder therefore replicates the last row and the last column of the
chunk until both dimensions satisfy this (one row and, for even widths,
one column for the standard 256-scanline chunk and power-of-two tiles;
at most 2^L - 1 otherwise), and the decoder discards the replicated
samples.  The padded size is carried by the SIZ marker and L by the
COD marker of the codestream, so the chunk header and the file format
are unchanged, and a codestream whose size equals the chunk size is
still accepted.  Lossless HTJ2K chunks and the planar (subsampled)
path are not affected.

Adds testLJ2KBoundary, which checks the rows and columns adjacent to
every chunk / tile boundary of smooth gradients (scanline and tiled,
including partial border tiles) and round-trips sizes around the
padding modulus, and documents the padding in the technical
introduction.

Signed-off-by: Osamu Watanabe <owatanab@es.takushoku-u.ac.jp>

* LJ2K: guard the padding arithmetic and fix the uncompressed fallback

Review follow-ups for the chunk-boundary padding:

- ht_padded_length() now works in int64_t, rejects a decomposition count
  above 30 (a codestream may carry up to 32, which would overflow the
  shift) and a padded length that no longer fits in a 32-bit dimension.
  The decoder treats either as a corrupt chunk; the encoder codes such a
  chunk unpadded, which is still a valid file.

- When the codestream does not fit in the uncompressed size, the chunk is
  now stored uncompressed by copying the packed samples into the
  compressed buffer, as the other codecs do.  Previously only the size
  was set and the buffer kept a truncated codestream; through the C API
  that produced a corrupt chunk (the C++ API has its own check).  The
  padding makes this case more likely for very small chunks.

Signed-off-by: Osamu Watanabe <owatanab@es.takushoku-u.ac.jp>

* LJ2K: bound the accepted decomposition count by the encoder's constant

The decoder accepted padded codestreams for up to 30 decomposition
levels, which allows a crafted codestream to declare an extent up to
2^30 - 1 rows and columns beyond the chunk size and so to sidestep the
image and tile size limits that were checked against the file header.

Make the number of levels written by the encoder a named constant,
HT_NUM_DECOMPS, and accept padded codestreams only up to that value.
The padding is then at most 2^HT_NUM_DECOMPS - 1 = 31 rows and columns,
a fixed margin that does not depend on file content.

Signed-off-by: Osamu Watanabe <owatanab@es.takushoku-u.ac.jp>
